source.title: Old Memories Die Hard: Unveiling Shallow Forgetting and Ripple Effects in Privacy Unlearning
source.authors: Xiaoyi Chen; Hao-Yu Wang; Si-Yuan Tang; Si-Jia Liu; Li-Ya Su; Xiao-Feng Wang; Hai-Xu Tang

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper, including appendices; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning against ICL and fine-tuning recovery attacks and presents evidence that label-based forgetting is shallow, while also reporting a representation-level refinement with incomplete recovery resistance.
record.gate_note: The study tests direct retrieval, ICL recovery, and fine-tuning recovery across unlearning methods. It also reports layer-wise CKA and utility results relevant to its explanation of shallow forgetting. Reported core-set-selection values and layer-selection values used to choose settings are not entered as result rows. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study runs direct retrieval (P1), 10-shot ICL (P2) and fine-tuning relearning (P3) attacks on 19 unlearning methods, including WHP and RMU from the original sources. It uses LLaMA-3.2-3B, LLaMA-3.1-8B and GPT-2-Large on Enron PII and TOFU. It shows near-zero P1 alongside 50–70% P3 recovery for label-based methods, and argues from layer-wise CKA that forgetting is shallow. This bears on whether unlearning works (A), recovery by fine-tuning (B), analysis-based recovery (C), ICL recovery (E) and robust counter-methods (F: SAM, RAU).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PII ripple effects are gradient-driven, not semantic. They also conclude that label-based unlearning is shallow, changing mainly the final layers, so PII stays recoverable by fine-tuning despite near-zero direct retrieval. Further points: SAM does not close the relearning gap; RAU narrows the gap without RMU's utility collapse but still leaks about 30%. They present RAU as a refinement, not a solution.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a suite of privacy-unlearning recipes, including GA, WHP, and RMU, under its own PII setup and active-attack protocol; it is not a reproduction of one original method's full recipe. It additionally introduces RAU.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies by unlearning method, known versus unknown forget set, dataset (Enron versus TOFU), model, fine-tuning budget, and representation-intervention layer. RAU's reported P3 depends on the starting layer; the paper reports worse recovery when starting at layers 16 or 24 than at 20.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning the known forget set spills over to unknown records. This spill-over correlates with gradient association (r=0.73 for GA) but not with social-graph PageRank (r=-0.05).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning's spill-over onto non-targeted memorized records follows gradient similarity, not semantic or relational structure.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026
record.problems: The primary reported PII evaluation uses Enron, with a smaller TOFU extension. Fine-tuning attacks use examples from the original forget set, so the results do not establish recovery from unrelated or loosely related examples. The paper states that results are averaged over 3 seeds and standard deviations are computed, but uncertainty values are not shown in the supplied result tables. Several layer-wise CKA values are conveyed through figures and accompanying descriptions.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted rows for other methods and metrics in Tables 1–4, SAM, GPT-2-Large, further RAU layer settings, and the gradient/representation association analyses to keep the extraction focused on the directly relevant recovery and layer-persistence results. These appear in Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendices C–F. The reported P1/P2 values for TOFU and the other per-method results in Tables 1 and 3 are also not separately extracted.

untested.parts: No WMDP-style multiple-choice accuracy or chance-level threshold; PII exact-match extraction only.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; attackers only fine-tune on other forget-set records.
Activation-direction ablation; only CKA analysis is done.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages; only 10-shot ICL with forget-set examples is tested.
Resistance of SAM/RAU to quantization, prompt attacks other than ICL, or unrelated-data relearning.

missing.what: SAM robust-unlearning results: P3 stays at 54–58% for GA/NPO and rises to 48.53% for RMU_SAM. Declared in rows_left_out, but central to version F.
Target model reference values: P3 60.60%, P2 29.94%; TOFU target P3 41.75%.
GPT-2-Large fixed-budget results: large P1–P3 gaps, e.g. GA P1 0% vs P3 22.68%.

record.verdict_notes: The relearning data are other forget-set records, excluding the queried record's own PII, so version B is tested only in its 'subset of forgotten facts' form. P3 is reported at per-method epoch budgets (3 or 10); GPT-2 uses a uniform 10 epochs. Results are averaged over 3 seeds, but no standard deviations are shown. RAU is the authors' own method, so F verdicts on it rest on self-evaluation. The reader's E support label wrongly cited r05/r06, which are P1 rows.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests direct retrieval, active recovery, and utility for its unlearning methods, but does not define or test chance-level performance as a formal threshold.
Fine-tuning uses examples from the original forget set, excluding the queried record. Unrelated or loosely related examples are not tested.
The study analyzes layer-wise representations and recovery, but does not ablate an activation direction.
Low-bit quantization attacks are not tested.
The study tests 10-shot ICL using examples from the forget set. Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and other prompt-only attacks are not tested.
RAU is evaluated under the study's ICL and fine-tuning attacks. The study does not test resistance to quantization, rephrasing, jailbreaks, or other languages.

reader_labels.label: challenges

reader_labels.reason: Direct retrieval is near zero, but fine-tuning recovery reaches 54.27%–65.98% in the reported known-set conditions and 54.68%–65.46% in unknown-set conditions (r01–r06, r17–r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: RMU has lower P3 recovery than label-based methods, but recovery remains measurable and its QA utility is very low on LLaMA-3.2-3B (r23, r24, r36, r40, r41).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GA, NPO, and DPO; fine-tuning with examples from the original forget set
reader_labels.reason: With 50 fine-tuning examples, the reported P3 rates are high after methods with near-zero direct retrieval (r17–r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: RMU and the TOFU known/unknown splits
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is lower for RMU and varies between known and unknown TOFU records, rather than restoring all records uniformly (r23, r24, r30–r33).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Label-based unlearning methods, especially GA, NPO, and DPO
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports largely unchanged early and middle layers alongside high fine-tuning recovery, consistent with surface suppression rather than deletion (r17–r22, r28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: These methods alter intermediate representations and lower recovery relative to label-based methods, although neither eliminates recovery and RMU incurs a utility cost (r23, r24, r27, r29, r36, r37).
